name: Risk aversion
definition_and_reason: Curvature of the old-age consumption certainty equivalent in V6 Epstein--Zin preferences, with unit intertemporal elasticity. The risk-aversion concept has an established empirical literature; transfer still requires compatible risks and population.
proposed_discipline: Review \lit{EZ}{EZ89} and \lit{BJKS}{BJKS97}, then document a range and aggregation assumptions. V6 theory additionally needs $0<\gamma<1$; retain contrary evidence rather than choosing only estimates that deliver bubbles. The solver accepts $\gamma>0$, while the displayed utility excludes $\gamma=1$.

name: Labor endowments
definition_and_reason: Masses of skilled and unskilled young workers; production uses $\varphi_iH_i$ and research uses $(1-\varphi_i)H_i$. These are external inputs registered as parameters, with credible labor-data counterparts.
proposed_discipline: Use the existing CPS/Eurostat mappings after fixing skill, age/cohort, sector and headcount/FTE definitions. Preserve relative country and skill sizes when choosing units. This is the data-based part of A; a search for a conventional literature number is unnecessary.

name: Inverse markup
definition_and_reason: Intermediate firms charge $p_i=w_{H,i}/\vartheta_i$, so their price/marginal-cost markup is $\mu_i=1/\vartheta_i$. The demand elasticity across varieties is $1/(1-\vartheta_i)$, distinct from the final-sector CES elasticity.
proposed_discipline: Review markup evidence such as \lit{DLEU}{DLEU20}; map a compatible gross markup by $\vartheta_i=1/\mu_i$. Distinguish markups from profit shares, overhead and taxes. A US listed-firm aggregate need not represent V6 intermediates or the RoW; retain sector/aggregation alternatives.

name: Final-sector CES curvature
definition_and_reason: For $F=[\alpha\widetilde X^{1-\rho}+(1-\alpha)\widetilde L^{1-\rho}]^{1/(1-\rho)}$, the substitution elasticity is $\sigma_i=1/\rho_i$. A clear transformation and substantial substitution literature make this a priority for external review.
proposed_discipline: Use \lit{KM}{KM92} and \lit{CC}{CC06} as related skill/technology evidence. Match the intermediate-input/unskilled-labor margin, markup and technology controls before transfer. The implemented restriction $\rho_{US}>1$ means $\sigma_{US}<1$ (complementarity), not substitutability.

name: OLG utility / saving weight
definition_and_reason: V6 places weights $1-\beta$ and $\beta$ on young consumption and the old-age certainty equivalent, yielding $A_t=\beta e_{US,t}$. A conventional annual infinite-horizon discount factor is a different object.
proposed_discipline: Use compatible life-cycle/OLG saving and preference evidence; \lit{HKT}{HKT25} is the closest specification. If a two-date utility instead uses weights $1,\delta$, then $\beta=\delta/(1+\delta)$. This algebra alone supplies no annual-to-generation conversion. Do not fit $\beta$ to an incompatible aggregate wealth/income ratio.

name: Unbalanced-regime persistence
definition_and_reason: $\pi=\Pr(z_{t+1}=u\mid z_t=u)$ with absorbing $b$. Its empirical interpretation needs an operational technology-regime definition and a model-period length. It also affects financial valuation, but is not a portfolio friction.
proposed_discipline: Use regime-duration or disaster literature (\lit{BARRO}{Barro06}) as an analogy, not a direct crash-probability estimate. Under a matched constant annual event probability $h$, $\pi=(1-h)^{\Delta}$ for a $\Delta$-year period. Without matched events, report scenarios and re-fit C across them; an all-$u$ sample alone is weak evidence.

name: Innovation productivity
assignment_status: External range from a joint mapping
definition_and_reason: $N_{i,t+1}/N_{i,t}-1=a_i(1-\varphi_{i,t})H_i$. R\&D productivity evidence is relevant, but V6 varieties and skilled research labor are not directly observed as a matched pair. The coefficient depends on labor units and period length.
proposed_discipline: Use \lit{BJRW}{BJRW20} and \lit{HKT}{HKT25} to organize evidence and specification alternatives. Discipline $a_iH_i$ jointly with knowledge growth and the research share; recover $a_i$ only after fixing $H_i$. A research-spending growth rate or a patent count does not by itself deliver $a_i$.

name: CES distribution weights
definition_and_reason: Levels enter through $\alpha_iA_{X,i}^{1-\rho_i}$ and $(1-\alpha_i)A_{L,i}^{1-\rho_i}$. A labor share is informative conditional on technology, markup and inputs; it is not the CES weight itself.
proposed_discipline: Fix units and a production normalization, then use matched income shares and relative wages, following the logic of \lit{CC}{CC06}. Do not separately choose both augmentation scales and $\alpha_i$ as if all three were independently identified. AHP cost shares use a different production model.

name: US productivity scales in u
definition_and_reason: $A^u_{X,US}=\bar A_{X,US,u}N_{US}^{\xi_u}$ and $A^u_{L,US}=\bar A_{L,US,u}N_{US}^{\nu_u}$. Code fields \code{A\_X\_US\_u}, \code{A\_L\_US\_u} are scale coefficients, not observed TFP levels.
proposed_discipline: Use initial output, matched skill wages and labor quantities under a declared $N_0$ and $\alpha$ normalization (\lit{CC}{CC06}; \lit{HKT}{HKT25}). Construct joint ranges for relative productivity and scale; record any production moments used to assign them as targeted moments.

name: US absorbing-regime scales
definition_and_reason: These levels determine post-switch production and equity payoffs. With $\nu_b=0$ they are constant augmentations. A history observed entirely in $u$ does not directly reveal the $b$ technology.
proposed_discipline: Use defensible post-transition analogues, bounded productivity changes or explicit continuity restrictions, with \lit{HKT}{HKT25} as a model comparison. Do not silently equate them to the $u$ scales. Re-fit C across these scenarios because switch severity trades off with $\pi$ and $\gamma$ in asset prices.

name: RoW productivity scales
definition_and_reason: With $\xi_W=0$, these are constant RoW factor augmentations, not country-average TFP. They set relative income and funding capacity and interact with $\alpha_W$, labor units and the geographic definition of RoW.
proposed_discipline: Use matched output and skill-wage evidence for the declared country aggregate; \lit{CC}{CC06} guides interpretation and \lit{AHP}{AHP25} the corporate-account scope. Keep full RoW and covered-country proxies distinct; a common scale normalization cannot determine all relative productivity levels.

name: Knowledge-spillover elasticities
definition_and_reason: These are elasticities of factor augmentations with respect to the knowledge stock: $\partial\log A_X/\partial\log N=\xi_u$, $\partial\log A_L/\partial\log N=\nu_u$. Broad innovation/growth estimates are related, but do not identify this pair directly.
proposed_discipline:
Combine \lit{HKT}{HKT25}, \lit{CC}{CC06} and \lit{BJRW}{BJRW20} with knowledge and wage-growth mappings. Report a joint range. The solver requires $\xi_u>
u_u\ge0$; V6 theory additionally uses $
u_u>
u_b$. $\psi_{US}=(\xi_u-
u_u)(ho_{US}-1)$ is derived, not another free parameter.

name: Fixed growth specialization
definition_and_reason: These technology coefficients are fixed at zero by this solver. B marks their model-specific family; the zeros are imposed restrictions, not estimates.
proposed_discipline: Retain and assess these restrictions. Positive-exponent scenarios, including related \lit{HKT}{HKT25} illustrations, require an alternative solver before any value search.

name: Equity-allocation friction
definition_and_reason: Curvature of $-\kappa(\omega-\bar\omega)^2/2$ and its RoW counterpart. It governs the response of portfolio shares to expected risk-adjusted relative equity returns. There is no portable standard home-bias cost for this utility normalization.
proposed_discipline: Use share/return variation and gross equity exposures, conditional on A/B. \lit{CR}{CR13} provides plausibility checks. A single observed share mainly restricts the combination $\kappa(\omega-\bar\omega)$; it does not separate $\kappa$ from the center. Consider a restricted C block if informative variation is insufficient.

name: US-equity preference centers
definition_and_reason: Both are preferred US-equity weights within an investor equity portfolio, for US and RoW investors respectively. They are distinct from actual $\omega,\omega^*$ and from foreign ownership of the US issuer sector.
proposed_discipline: Use AHP-style gross equity positions and conditional portfolio-weight mappings jointly with $\kappa$ (\lit{AHP}{AHP25}; \lit{CR}{CR13}). Neither $E_L/V_{US}$ nor one observed home-bias index directly measures either center. Full RoW wealth/value coverage remains a constraint for $\omega^*$.

name: Foreign demand for US safe claims
definition_and_reason: Coefficient of RoW utility from US-bond holdings; it also changes RoW saving to $A^*=[(\beta+\chi)/(1+\chi)]e_W$. Its value depends on the utility normalization and wealth/claim definitions.
proposed_discipline: Combine foreign safe-claim holdings, matched wealth/saving evidence and suitable safe-asset spreads. \lit{KVJ}{KVJ12} supports the convenience-yield mechanism, not a V6 coefficient value. AHP net non-equity positions are useful accounting targets but are not automatically pure safe debt.

name: US bond-share friction
definition_and_reason: Scales the utility term $-\eta\Upsilon(\theta)$ with the code-imposed $\Upsilon(\theta)=-\log(1-\theta)+\theta^2/2$. It is not an observed bond underwriting fee or a resource cost.
proposed_discipline: Jointly use US net borrowing, its response to returns, and the safe-return wedge, conditional on $\chi$, $\beta$ and the chosen bond mapping. External financing-friction studies offer plausibility only. NFA, CA and valuation alone need not separately identify $\eta$ and $\chi$.
